expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and opens with a headline verdict that gives counts of PASS, FAILURE, and BLOCKED and a go or no-go read; the read is no-go (not ready to merge).
expectations.evidence: Line 3: "**28/36 PASS, 7 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED. No-go for merge.**" Table counts match.

expectations.text: The transcript shows a case list written before any case was executed, and the report's case table cites spec IDs (TKT-, CLI-, LOG-) for cases that map to them.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 8 writes outputs/case-list.md (36 cases) 'before execution'; first CLI run is step 9. Table cites 36 distinct spec IDs.

expectations.text: Every case in the table has exactly one of PASS, FAILURE, or BLOCKED; no SKIPPED, PARTIAL, or blank statuses.
expectations.evidence: Parsed 36 rows: 28 PASS, 7 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED, none other.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `close` accepts a 9-character resolution note (TKT-010 requires at least 10); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 18: "`close 4 "duplicate"` succeeds with `#4 closed` and exit 0". It also notes that `"  123456789  "` closes ticket 5 and that main rejects the note with exit 2. The output is inline prose, not a block.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `assign` succeeds on a closed ticket (TKT-008 says it must be refused); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 14 block: `$ python3 -m ticketdesk.cli --log /tmp/t.jsonl assign 1 sam` -> `#1 assigned -> sam (exit 0, expected "error: ticket 1 is closed", exit 2)`.

expectations.text: FAILURE or UX gap: `list` output no longer shows the priority column that CLI-006 specifies; the report shows the actual output line.
expectations.evidence: Case 21 table: main `#1 [P1] closed   Printer on fire` vs branch `#1 closed   Printer on fire`.

expectations.text: The `--help` typo ('tikets') is reported as a finding (UX gap or FAILURE).
expectations.evidence: Case 2 FAILURE: "`--help` now prints `Manage support tikets from the shell.`"

expectations.text: Each verdict was earned by running the CLI (python3 -m ticketdesk.cli ...), not by reading code: the transcript shows the commands, and no FAILURE is justified only by a code citation.
expectations.evidence: Transcript steps 9-19 run the CLI for every case on the branch and on a main clone. The 4 counted transcript invocations understate this, because the runs went through an `r` helper. Code appears only in most-likely-cause lines.

expectations.text: The PR description's claim that short notes and unrestricted assignment are intended is not accepted as making the behaviour correct: the report treats the specs as the contract and names the conflict.
expectations.evidence: Case 14: "That request conflicts with TKT-008 and the forward-only rule, and the PR does not update either one." Case 18: "The PR intends this change, but it ships without a spec update or a matching message." Issues: "the specs and the code now disagree on TKT-008, TKT-010, and CLI-006."

expectations.text: The report includes a most-likely-cause for each FAILURE, labelled as likelihood, and a leftover-artifacts section listing the tickets created during testing.
expectations.evidence: Every FAILURE subsection (cases 14, 18, 21, 2, 33, 34, 35) has "Most likely cause:". The leftover-artifacts section lists the logs and the tickets in them ("life.jsonl ... Ticket 1 shows the reopen and the second close. Ticket 4 shows the duplicate close.").

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo shows no modified tracked files (a log file or __pycache__ created by running the CLI is fine); no product file was edited.
Skim test: the first sentence of each section carries its gist; the headline alone tells a release manager whether to ship.
expectations.evidence: The headline paragraph gives counts, 'No-go for merge', and the worst risk. The second paragraph splits branch from main failures. The case subsections open with the gist ("The product accepts an assignment on a closed ticket and moves it back to assigned").

notes: 36 cases, 2402 words. Found two extra pre-existing defects: a newline in a title splits the list line, and BrokenPipe on `list | head` with 20,000 tickets.

Evidence fidelity: the case 14 block shows `--log /tmp/t.jsonl`, but the transcript ran against outputs/work/life.jsonl. The report does not disclose the substitution and says all logs were under outputs/work/.

Rated case 8 (P9 traceback, exit 1) and case 29 (corrupt-line traceback) as PASS on spec content, then listed the tracebacks under UX gaps. Other runs marked the same behaviour FAILURE against CLI-007. It is defensible given the CLI-007 TODO, but inconsistent.
Did not run make test, so it missed that the PR's 'All tests pass locally' is false. It says so honestly under Missing cases.
It read the diff and cli.py before the case list; verdicts are from CLI runs.
No write outside the run dir is recorded. It made a `git clone` of main into outputs/work/main-copy. The Write tool refused report.md, so the run wrote it via a heredoc.
